Question: Which method appears to be most robust to the presence of outliers in the training data?
Evidence:
[E1] (figure, Figure 6, page 7) (image attached): Figure 6: (a-c) Average ﬁtting errors while varying the outlier rates and (e-f) ﬁtting results of the compared methods with 60% outliers using cosexp , linear , and step functions.
Words printed in the figure: (a) (b) (c) (d) (e) (f)
[E2] (figure, Figure 6, page 7): a zoomed view of Figure 6 (image attached) [image]

claims.text: Figure 6 shows the average fitting errors while varying the outlier rates for cosexp, linear, and step functions.

cites.quote: Figure 6: (a-c) Average ﬁtting errors while varying the outlier rates and (e-f) ﬁtting results of the compared methods with 60% outliers using cosexp , linear , and step functions.

claims.text: In the average error plots (a-c), the proposed method maintains the lowest average error across varying outlier rates for all tested functions.

cites.quote: Figure 6: (a-c) Average ﬁtting errors while varying the outlier rates

cites.observation: In subfigures (a), (b), and (c), the blue line representing the Proposed method stays lowest and flattest as the Outlier rate increases from 0.0 to 0.6 compared to MDN, MLP, and Robust methods.
